about: What changed in Pyr, for players. Newest first. Every deploy that changes something a player can see or do adds an entry at the top: 'at' is when it went live (UTC), the title names it, and each item is one plain sentence a player would understand, with no code words. The game shows these in the 'New version ready' notice. See CHANGELOG-RULE in README.md.

entries.title: A new padlock
items: Locked datasets in the Dataset switcher, and the note on a view you can't open yet, show Pyr's own padlock. When an admin gives you access to a dataset, your note says so with the padlock open.

entries.title: Super Quests on MEC, and your time on each cell
items: MEC has Super Quests: help discover giant interneurons, cell types that have never been mapped before. They are under a new Super Quests chip in the Cell Library, and one can take weeks, a little at a time.
You may hold one Super Quest at a time, beside your other claims, for up to 2 months.
A Super Quest has three marks: AIS, which is required, Checked and True End.
Hide marks, in Marks on MEC cells, hides the mark layers so you can see the cell, and Show marks brings them back.
Your Super Quest is also at the top of My Cells.
Marks says when you started working on the cell, and for a Super Quest, the day it is yours until. In its last week, Pyr reminds you that it is ending.
Admins can set each Super Quest's soma point in Admin Hub.
My Week in Science shows your time on Super Quests, and so do the month and year recaps.
Pyr congratulates you at 10, 25, 50 and 100 hours of active time on one cell, and when you finish a Super Quest.
Find ends at the edge is put away for now on MEC cells, and Pyr no longer places Hits Edge marks by itself.

Each MEC claim shows your active time on it, such as 14 h 20 min so far. It counts while the cell is on screen, Pyr is in front, and you have done real work on it in the last 5 minutes: a mark, an annotation or highlight, a merge or split, or Save view. It adds up across visits and devices.

entries.title: Highlight stays open after a refresh
items: If the Highlight box was open when you refreshed the page, it opens again, as merge and cut mode do. Thanks to Nik.

entries.title: Slim view for Quests
items: In the Cell Library's Quests tab, the slim view now shrinks to the quest cell you are working on, with its Save, Open and Submit buttons. With slim view on, opening the Quests tab goes straight there. Thanks to toknow.

entries.title: Ask for access to a dataset
items: A dataset you can't open now has a Request access button, on its card in the Dataset switcher and on a note that appears when a view opens on it (from a chat link, say). The admins are told, and you get a note when they answer.

Production data comes in levels: the retina is Level 1, unlocked with retina edit access (send your edits from Ask for Edit Access). Medial Entorhinal Cortex is Level 2: once Level 1 is unlocked, you can ask for it.
The Sandbox card in the Dataset switcher has one button, Start here, which opens the tutorial you are on, or the next one.

entries.title: Extension Sandbox fixes
items: Every Extension Sandbox cell now opens on the cell alone, close in on where it stops early.
Help me shows the missing pieces along with their gems, and a stray hint point is gone.
Moving on to the next cell says so while the last one is put back, instead of waiting without a word.

entries.title: Merges that are not the missing piece
items: In the Merge tutorial and the Extension Sandbox, a merge that goes through but is not one of the pieces the exercise asks for now says so, instead of leaving the count unchanged without a word.

entries.title: Chat tips
items: A new ? at the top of chat opens a short card of everything chat can do. Typing /help opens it too.
Saying @nurro now gets a private answer from Nurro pointing you to its ! commands, and !help mentions the chat tips.

entries.title: Actions in chat, and when your cells were last saved
items: Type /me and an action in chat, like /me claps hands, and it shows as a grey line with your name.
In My Cells, your other claims show when their view was last saved.
In Highlight, the button that shrinks the box stays at the left when the box is open.

entries.title: One notification feed, bigger Achievements, and a Settings key
items: Your notifications are back in one feed. To sort them into My Pyr and Pyr Updates, turn on Organize my notifications into categories in Settings.
Your profile shows your three most recent Achievements in each row, bigger.
Press Shift and S to open Settings. You can also add a Settings gear to your top bar in Settings.

entries.title: Help build the next Hunt
items: Some Sandbox cells are now Hunt candidates: they are listed first in the Cell Library, under a new Hunt chip, for you to claim and proofread fully. A claim on one lasts 24 hours.

When a candidate is proofread, players with production access can suggest the errors for a Hunt: open Help build in the top bar, then Cut or Merge as you normally would. Pyr checks each one would work and keeps it as your suggestion, and the cell stays as it is.
Press Send to the admins when you are done. Everyone whose suggestion is planted earns the Hunt Maker Achievement when the Hunt ends.
Cells being made into a Hunt are hidden until it starts, and cannot be claimed or edited.

entries.title: Drag the Pasted list taller
items: The Pasted list in the Segments tab has a grip under it, like a folder's: drag it to make the list taller or shorter, and double click it for the usual size. Your height is remembered.

entries.title: FlyWire tour: one stray T4 cell left out
items: Show all T4a cells in the FlyWire tour no longer includes one cell whose body sits outside the brain, far from the rest. FlyWire labels it T4a, but it is not a good one to look at. Thanks to wolfryder101.

entries.title: Bigger Achievements, and small fixes in chat and Highlight
items: Your Trophy Case shows Achievements bigger. Point at one to see its name.
In a narrow chat, the emoji and reaction pickers now stay on the screen.
In Highlight, after your first mark the box tells you the next step: click another spot to highlight between.

entries.title: MEC: the AIS is ready to confirm
items: On MEC cells, the lab's sheet now has the AIS, where the axon leaves the cell. In Marks, pick AIS and Go to the lab's AIS point. If it is off, move the crosshairs. Confirm AIS here puts the mark where the crosshairs are.
Confirm soma here also puts the Soma mark where the crosshairs are, and confirming again moves the mark.
An Axon complete cell is now labelled axon complete in the lab's records, apart from fully proofread cells.

entries.title: A little cheer for a solved help request
items: When you mark a help request solved, a short Solved! card with Nurro says thanks and that it moved to Resolved.

entries.title: Lantern: Clicked branch, smoother
items: A small gem marks where you clicked while Pyr finds the branch, and the Lantern bar shows that it is working.
The lit branch is now lit all along, with no dark patches.
Only the cell you clicked lights up; other cells passing through stay dark.

entries.title: The Eyewire II Principles
items: The first time you open the retina dataset, Pyr asks you to agree to the Eyewire II Principles: keep what you find within the community and respect each other's work. One click, once.

entries.title: Lantern: Clicked branch fixes
items: In Clicked branch, the cell now waits in shadow until you click a branch.
A click lights just the branch you clicked, not most of the cell.
Clicking empty space puts the light out again.

entries.title: React with the Pyr gem, and a tidier view corner
items: In chat you can now react to a message with the Pyr gem, first in the row of reactions.
The x y z letters in the top left of each view are hidden. To bring them back, tick xyz top left in Settings, in the Neuroglancer box.

entries.title: Lantern: Clicked branch
items: The Lantern has a new choice, Clicked branch: click a branch and only that branch lights up, from where it forks off out to its tips.
Click another branch to move the light, or click empty space to bring the normal view back.
Whole cell is still the usual Lantern, and stays the default.

entries.title: MEC: proofread the axon only
items: On MEC, proofread just the axon now, from the AIS to every one of its ends, and ignore missed spines.
When the axon is done, Complete the cell and choose Axon complete: it counts as your completed cell and goes into the lab's sheet. Proofread the whole cell? Choose Complete instead.

entries.title: Hunt results order
items: A Hunt's results now rank by medal, then most found, then fewest gems.
Achievement notes in the bell are tidier.

entries.title: Hunt box tidy
items: The Hunt box's title bar stays put while you scroll it.
Watch it grow is off for a running Hunt's cells, so it can't give away the answers.

entries.title: Hunt reports
items: When a problem you sent with Found a problem the Hunt missed is added to the answers, you hear it in the bell.

entries.title: Hunt box tidy
items: Sending a problem the Hunt missed now shows a green Sent and a thank you.
The Hunt box shows hours and minutes, and the seconds in the last hour; the top bar keeps the seconds.

entries.title: Report a problem the Hunt missed
items: Found a real merger or missing extension the Hunt does not have? In the Hunt box, press "Found a problem the Hunt missed?", put the crosshair on it, choose Cut or Merge, and send it to the admins. No gem is used, and if it is real you get Laser Eyes.
The Hunt countdown keeps the same width as the seconds tick.

entries.title: Hunt fixes
items: The Hunt countdown now shows seconds, so you can see it running.
Click "missed" under your gem dots to see every gem that missed, go to each one, and tell the admins if one is on a real problem.
Going back a page in your browser no longer fills the console with errors while the cells load.

entries.title: Tell the admins about a problem the Hunt missed
items: When a Hunt gem says "Not there" but you are sure it is on a real merger or missing extension, press "It's real: tell the admins". An admin checks it, and if it is real it counts for you, with Laser Eyes.

entries.title: Laser Eyes, and Hunt answers that are bigger than a point
items: Laser Eyes is a new Hunt Achievement: find a real merger or missing extension that the Hunt's answers missed, and once an admin checks it, it counts for you. You can earn it once in each Hunt, and your profile counts them up.
A Hunt answer can now be a whole area, like a wide flat end, so a gem anywhere on it counts.
New lines for the Gold, Silver and Bronze Achievements, from Celia.

entries.title: The Hunt box opens faster
items: The Hunt box finds the Hunt much faster when it opens.
A Hunt's card in chat says where the Hunt is now: "The Hunt is on" while it runs and "The Hunt is over" after, and only its newest card stays in chat.

entries.title: Hits Edge found for you on MEC
items: Pyr now marks Hits Edge on its own wherever an MEC cell reaches the end of the imaged data, using the lab's image mask, once the cell has loaded in 3D. Check each one.
Find ends at the edge in Marks looks again, with a bar showing how far it has got, and Undo in Marks takes back the newest mark, or every mark one search placed.
Claiming or opening an MEC cell no longer adds extra copies of the Can't Fix layer, and copies already there are folded back into one, keeping their points.

entries.title: See the answers after a Hunt
items: When a Hunt is over, Show the answers in the Hunt box puts a ring on every merger and missing extension, so you can see the ones you missed.
Your own gems stay where you dropped them, so a ring with no gem on it is one you did not find.

entries.title: Tell us your EyeWire name when you ask to join
items: When you ask to join Pyr, you can now add your EyeWire username and rank if you played EyeWire.

entries.title: Reviewing access requests: two more
items: Pointing at or clicking a point in the 2D or 3D view lights up that point in the review box's list.
The answer you are writing to a requester in the Admin Hub is kept while you go and review their examples, until you send it.
Thanks to Celia for both.

entries.title: Calm screen no longer blanks the page
items: With Calm screen on in Settings, Pyr opened to a black page since the Hunt arrived. It now opens as it should, with the Hunt's effects calmed.
Thanks to Krzysztof for finding exactly what was hiding it.

entries.title: Hunt fixes from the first Hunt
items: Top hunters now updates for everyone about every half minute while a Hunt runs. Before, you only saw your own row move.
The Gems box shows the gems you have left, and a line under it says how many you used: how many were right and how many missed. Thanks to Nseraf for spotting that it did not add up.
A color key under the Hunt instructions says what each gem color means, and what the teal glow on a cell means.
Take back removes your last gem before you press Submit. Gems that are already checked stay where they are.
Cut and Extend follow the gem layer you pick, and their tooltips name the number key that switches between them.
A Hunt cell that would be drawn teal gets another color, so teal always means the edge of the dataset.
In the small Hunt box, Cut and Extend stay readable beside Submit.

entries.title: A shorter line in Settings
items: The Neuroglancer box in Settings now simply says: Neuroglancer's own controls and panels.

entries.title: Trophies for the Champions
items: Monthly Champions now has its own gold and violet look: gold, silver and bronze neuron cups for the top editors, and neuron awards for the top cell completers.
Weekly Champions has a trophy of its own too: a gem held by a golden neuron.
Opening Weekly or Monthly Champions sets off blue, purple and yellow confetti behind it.
Weekly Champions now counts the week Monday to Sunday on US Eastern time, like Your Week in Science.
Your Month in Science shows the whole community's edits and cells for that month.
Each month's top three editors and top three cell completers win a trophy that joins Competitions in their profile, and each winner gets a note in My Pyr.

entries.title: Fixes to reviewing access requests
items: Reviewing an access request: the points now show on every example you jump to, and clicking a point takes you to it instead of off into empty space.
The review box has a close button that ends the review and takes its points away, and a long list of points scrolls inside the box instead of running off the bottom of the screen.
Thanks to Celia for all four.

entries.title: Gems and points back to their normal size
items: Some players had every gem and annotation point drawn extra large, from an old size setting that is no longer in Settings. That old setting no longer applies; each annotation layer's Size slider sets its own points.
Thanks to Celia for reporting it.

entries.title: Minimize the Merge Queue
items: The Merge Queue has a minimize button: it folds into the Merge Mode bar as Merge Queue with the number of pairs, and one click opens it again. It stays minimized after a reload and on other datasets.
Merge and Cut mode now stay behind your profile, Submit an issue and other full windows instead of showing on top of them.
Thanks to Krzysztof for both ideas.

entries.title: A warmer welcome while you wait to join
items: If Pyr is still invite only for you, the music no longer starts behind the waiting screen.
After you ask to join, the waiting screen thanks you and suggests things to do meanwhile: play EyeWire, or learn about the brain on connectome.quest.
You can now ask to join Pyr from connectome.quest too, without signing in first.

entries.title: Easier to read Help tab
items: In the Cell Library Help tab, the dataset names and the Resolved list are larger and easier to read.

entries.title: The \ key is just for the top bar
items: The \ key no longer opens a panel of loading statistics. It only brings down the Magic Top Bar.

entries.title: The Hunt
items: The Hunt is here: a timed event where everyone searches the same cells for mistakes. Watch your notifications and the top bar: each Hunt is announced before it starts.

Drop a gem on each merger you find (Cut) or each branch that stops short (Extend). You have a set number of gems, so choose carefully. Each gem is checked as it lands, or switch that off and press Submit when you are ready.
Where a cell runs out of the data, it glows teal. That is the edge of the dataset, not a missing branch, and a gem there costs nothing. You can turn the glow off in the Hunt box.

Gold, Silver and Bronze medals go to everyone who finds enough, and the fastest hunter wins the Speed award. Your medals show next to your Special Awards and in the Competitions section of your Trophy Case.

entries.title: Small fixes
items: Long top bar menus now scroll instead of running off the bottom of the window.
The Achievement window shows its title in the right font again, and the Ultramicrotome Achievement has a new line.
The close button of your profile now sits on the tab row, so the page has more room.

entries.title: Highlights take far less room
items: A highlight now saves as a few smooth lines instead of hundreds of tiny ones, so a saved view with lots of highlights is up to a hundred times smaller and always fits.
Highlights you made before are made smaller the same way when you open them; they look and work as before.

entries.title: Magic Top Bar
items: A new switch in Settings, under Screen: Magic Top Bar. The views get the whole window, and the top bar comes down when you move the mouse to the top edge or press the \ key.
While the bar is hidden, your unread notifications show as a small bell in the corner of the 3D view, and the Pyr gem sits at the left of the layer tabs.
Top bar icons now grow a little when you point at them.
Thanks to Nik for both ideas.

entries.title: Your cell keeps its highlights
items: The cell you are working on now saves its own view as you go (a little after you stop, and when you leave the tab), so reopening it brings back all your highlights, even after a reload.

entries.title: Your Month in Science and Monthly Champions
items: On the 1st of each month you get Your Month in Science in My Pyr: your edits, cells completed, achievements, best streak and your place for the month that just ended.
Opening it shows that whole month in your profile, counted on US Eastern time like the weekly one.
Monthly Champions arrives in Pyr Updates on the 1st, with the month's top editors and top cell completers.

entries.title: Neater pumpkin card buttons
items: The buttons on the pumpkin card now line up, edge to edge.

entries.title: Your Week in Science counts every edit
items: Busy weeks and months showed far too few edits in Your Week in Science (one player saw 24 for a month of over 20,000). It now counts all of them, and cells completed the way the leaderboard does.
Opening the Sunday Your Week in Science notification now shows that week, not the new one, and every week and month runs on US Eastern time, like the notification.

entries.title: Your share of the week, never 0%
items: Your Week in Science shows a small share of the community's edits as 0.1% or under 0.1%, instead of 0%.

entries.title: Smaller hint gems
items: The gems that show where to click in the tutorials and sandboxes are about half the size they were.

entries.title: A tidier Merge tutorial
items: The Merge tutorial is shorter to read, and both merges bring the view in close on the spots to click.
If you switch merge mode off partway, the box asks you to press M to turn it back on.
On the second merge the box sits low, so it no longer covers the cell.

entries.title: Pumpkins that grow, and another round
items: The Sandbox pumpkins now grow in over their cells once the cells have loaded, and the hammer bar counts them in while they grow.
When every pumpkin is smashed, the bar offers Again? to grow them back for another round.

entries.title: The Cell Library opens faster
items: On Retina the Cell Library now loads the first 100 cells of a tab, with a Load more button at the bottom for the next 100, instead of every cell at once. My Cells still shows all of your cells.
The tab counts, Claim a new cell, Claim 10 and the search still cover every cell in the dataset.

entries.title: Watch a cell grow
items: The Δ menu has a Watch it grow button. It opens a slider through every edit of the cell, oldest first, and shows the cell as it was at each one in the 3D view, including branches that were still separate pieces before they were joined on.

Each step says whether pieces were joined or cut off, who did it and when. The piece joined on shows in yellow and a piece cut off in red, so small edits stand out. Edits by lab members who are not Pyr players show as unknown.
Press Play to step through on its own, at the speed you choose, for screen recordings. Closing the panel shows today's cell again.
A bit cut out of another merger and joined on later shows on its own before it joins, without the rest of that merger.
A cell with hundreds of edits shows 150 of them, spread evenly from first to last.

entries.title: Photo mode: sharper recordings, MP4 and GIF, fades
items: Record spin in photo mode now keeps the thin branches of cells, which used to come out dotted or missing, most of all with a whole class on screen.
Recordings are saved as MP4, which plays in VLC and most other players, or as a small looping GIF for the forum.
Photo mode can turn the cell left and right or over the top.
Speed changes are gradual, and you choose how many seconds they take.
Fade in and Fade out make the cells appear or disappear slowly, and a recording follows what you do while it turns.

entries.title: My Pyr and Pyr Updates
items: The bell has two tabs: My Pyr for what was sent to you (replies, achievements, your week, your results), and Pyr Updates for news for everyone. It opens on the tab with the newest unread one.
Pyr Updates older than 5 days count as read, so the daily updates do not pile up, and Mark all read clears both tabs.
In Settings: Show all notifications in one list, and Show Today in Pyr daily updates.

entries.title: A tidier pumpkin card, and a wink
items: The pumpkin button in chat now always opens the pumpkin card, with Hide the pumpkin, Go to the patch, and Smash the pumpkins.
The chat emoji list has a wink.

entries.title: Smash the pumpkins
items: Grab a hammer and smash the Sandbox pumpkins: press Ctrl+K and type smash, or use Smash the pumpkins on the pumpkin card.
Each pumpkin you hit breaks into pieces. Once they are smashed they stay off until you press the pumpkin button in chat.

entries.title: A note on neuroglancer's old controls
items: In Settings, the switch for neuroglancer's controls button now says that its list is out of date for Pyr, and where to find Pyr's own keyboard shortcuts.

entries.title: Help reminders say which request
items: The Was your help request answered? note now shows what you asked, on which cell, and the reply, with buttons to mark it solved and to open the helper's view.

entries.title: Tidier Settings, Large text, and a fourth pumpkin
items: Settings are sorted into small boxes by topic: 3D looks, Screen, Jumping and views, 2D images, and Chat and notifications. Every setting works as before.
A new Neuroglancer box gathers the switches that bring back neuroglancer's own controls. Click its (i) to read what neuroglancer is.
A new Large text switch in Settings, under Screen, makes the text in Pyr's windows, the Cell Library, the bell and the side panel bigger.
A fourth jack o' lantern has appeared in the Sandbox pumpkin patch, and the pumpkin card has a Hide the pumpkin button.

entries.title: A note while the servers are down
items: While our data server is down, a note at the top says so. Merging and cutting still work.

entries.title: Chat no longer asks you to log in when you are
items: If the server was busy for a moment when you signed in, Pyr now tries again for your profile, instead of leaving chat saying Log in to chat until you reloaded.

entries.title: Pick how each cell ended
items: Completing a cell no longer starts with your last answer to How did it end? picked. You choose each time, so a wrong one cannot slip through.

entries.title: Clearer annotation tools
items: In an annotation layer, the Pyr gem comes first, the box, line, ellipse and polyline sit on a line of their own under the points, and the tool you pick is the one lit up.

entries.title: My Cells buttons stay in place
items: In My Cells, Save view now comes first, so the jump, Release and Complete buttons sit in the same place on every row.

entries.title: Cell & Quest celebration switch
items: In Settings, the cell and Quest message is now one switch, Cell & Quest celebration, beside Achievement celebration. Both are on unless you turn them off.

entries.title: Annotation folders keep your place
items: Opening, closing or hiding an annotation folder no longer throws the list down to the bottom; it stays where you were.

entries.title: Merge and cut stay open through a refresh
items: If merge or cut was open when you refreshed, it opens again once the cell has loaded, with your points still there.

entries.title: Quieter celebrations, if you like
items: Settings has a new Achievement celebration switch. Turn it off and achievements no longer pop up with a card and confetti; they are still in your Trophy Case and the bell.
Submitting a Quest cell now follows the When I complete a cell or a Quest setting, so Nothing really means nothing.

entries.title: No stray glow on cells
items: Points in a Soma, True End, Can't Fix or Hits Edge layer no longer glow on the cell outside MEC. On Retina they showed as a colored patch, as if highlighted.

entries.title: The Lantern bar stays behind your profile
items: Lantern's bar, and the Highlight, Batch and Quests boxes, now tuck behind the profile and the other full-screen windows instead of showing on top of them.

entries.title: Marks open on MEC claims
items: Marks under your MEC claim in the Cell Library are open from the start. Close them and they stay closed in this browser.

entries.title: Number keys pick a layer
items: A number key, 1 to 9, now makes that layer the active one, and Shift + the number shows or hides it. Each layer tab says its keys when you point at it.
Classic Layers (Click to hide) in Settings puts both back the old way: a click or a number hides or shows a layer.
Settings can hide the EyeWire Radio speaker in the corner.

entries.title: Mark MEC cells for the lab
items: Under the MEC cell you are working on, the Cell Library has Marks: pick Soma, AIS, True End, Can't Fix or Hits Edge and Ctrl + click the cell to place it, and see what is placed and what is still missing.
In Marks, a lab layer's number key picks its mark, so you can switch marks without clicking.
The soma is quick: the starting point is the nucleus, so Go to the starting point, check it is in the soma, and Confirm soma here.
Highlight opens on MEC too, with the same lab marks, and your highlight colors mark spots: one click, and the spot glows on the cell in its color.
When you complete an MEC cell, the Complete form lists the marks, and the lab's sheet gets how many of each you placed.

entries.title: Sandboxes keep your progress on a cell
items: In the Merger and Extension Sandboxes, pressing Next before you are done now says what is left and keeps your work. It used to put the cell back, so a half finished cell had to be done again.
The Extension Sandbox starts with the easy cell, one merge, before the one that needs two.

entries.title: The Cell Library comes back after a refresh, and tidier Find Path boxes
items: Refresh the page with the Cell Library open and it opens again on the same tab, still slimmed to the cell you were on.
In Find Path, the start and end points each sit on one short line, labelled source and target.

entries.title: The merge and cut bar no longer covers the Segments list
items: While merging or cutting, the side panel ends above the tool bar, so the last cells in the Segments list can be reached.

entries.title: Your country and bio follow you to a new browser
items: Sign in on a browser you have not used before and your profile shows your country and bio, instead of looking empty.

entries.title: The Selection box stays shut while you merge and cut
items: Placing merge and cut points no longer throws the Selection box open (it often said Annotation not found). It still opens for your own annotation layers.

entries.title: Open a help request in its own window
items: In the Cell Library, the new pop out button on a help request opens it in its own window, so the question is easy to read.
The window shows who asked, the cell, the question, their picture and every reply, with buttons to reply, jump to the cell and mark it solved.
Drag the window by its top bar and resize it from its corner. It remembers where you put it.
Thanks to annkri for the idea.

entries.title: Annotation folders you can place into and hide
items: Click the target on an annotation folder and every annotation you place goes into that folder. Click it again to stop.
Click a folder's eye to hide its annotations in the 2D and 3D views, handy for a part of a big cell you are finished with. They stay in the list, dimmed.
Thanks to annkri for the idea.

entries.title: Find Path stops when you close it
items: Closing Find Path stops a path still being traced. A path that takes too long now gives up after a minute or so (a minute and a half with Precision mode) and says what to try, instead of tracing forever.

entries.title: Pasted coordinates find the cell in 3D only
items: Paste coordinates into the Segments box while only the 3D view is showing, and the cell there loads: split screen opens for a moment to look, then goes back.

entries.title: Team up is resting for now
items: Team up and the Teams tab are put away for now.

entries.title: MEC cells come with their layers
items: Claim an MEC cell and it opens with the AIS, True End, Can't Fix and Hits Edge layers ready, and the Cell Library's instructions for MEC are in the game.

entries.title: Edits count after an outage
items: If the Pyr server is down for a while, your splits and merges from that time still count once it is back, for up to three days.

entries.title: A tighter menu that scrolls
items: The menu is tighter, and it scrolls when your window is too short to show all of it.
MEC's Cell Library no longer starts with an empty entry.
Announcements in chat no longer start with a megaphone; they have their picture.

entries.title: A ninth merger, a harder one
items: The Merger Sandbox has a ninth merger: two branches crossing in an X, with no clear border between them.

entries.title: Meet the cells of the retina
items: New in the Cell Library on Retina: Meet the cells, one example of each of the 117 cell types identified in the Eyewire II dataset, most common first.
Click a type to see its cell alone in 3D and turn it, or show a whole class, or all 117, together in their places in the retina, each type in its own color.
Each class comes with a short note on what it does, and Back to my view puts your own view back.

entries.title: Claim buttons only where you can claim
items: In Switch Dataset, the Available cells, Quests and My cells buttons now show only on datasets where you can claim cells.

entries.title: The window you click comes to the front
items: Click into chat and it comes in front of the Cell Library; click the Cell Library and it comes back in front. The same goes for the other floating windows.

entries.title: Pyr is invite only for now
items: Players who are not in the beta yet see a short form after signing in, where they can ask to join with their name, email and an optional note.

entries.title: A third cell in the Extension Sandbox
items: The Extension Sandbox has a new easy cell: an axon to extend by one piece. The black spill cell is now third.

entries.title: Bigger text when replying to a help request
items: In the Cell Library's Help tab, the box where you write a reply, the view link box and their buttons now use larger, easier to read text.

entries.title: A clearer Get Started tutorial
items: Get Started has new wording, the key and mouse actions in bold, and a small mouse picture showing which button to use.
The 2D EM tab glows when the tutorial asks you to open it, and the hint points no longer show twice.
Merge and Cut are switched off during Get Started, so the lesson stays the same for everyone. It now ends with a clear finish and the Merge tutorial.
The burger menu opens in front of the tutorial box.
The Extension Sandbox has a second cell: extending a branch through a black spill.

entries.title: The Extension Sandbox, and an eighth merger
items: New in the burger menu: the Extension Sandbox. Each cell stops too soon, with the rest of it left behind as separate pieces. Find where it ends early and merge the missing pieces back on.
The Merger Sandbox has an eighth merger to cut.

entries.title: Help replies take you to the request, and Assists
items: Open in Help tab on a reply to your help request now opens that request, highlighted, even when it is on another dataset.
The Help tab has All requests and Mine, so you can see just your own requests.
Assists on a profile now counts the other players' help requests you replied to, one each, and shows on every player's profile.
On a short screen the profile Overview scrolls instead of cutting off the Scout Report and your cells.

entries.title: Cut tutorial waits for both red points
items: In the Cut tutorial, Now press G comes up once both red points are placed, as the step asks, not after the first.

entries.title: No empty help requests
items: A help request needs a few words or a screenshot before it is sent, so a stray Enter in the help box no longer posts an empty request to chat.

entries.title: Straight to the work from Switch Dataset
items: In Switch Dataset, the Retina, MEC and Sandbox cards now have buttons that take you straight to Available cells, your own cells or Quests. One click switches if needed and opens the Cell Library on that tab, after you are signed in and the dataset is on screen.

entries.title: Picture notes show the picture big
items: A notification with just a title and a picture now shows the title on top and the picture across the whole window, like a video note.

entries.title: Today in Pyr counts what players did
items: The daily Today in Pyr note now shows how many edits players made and how many cells they completed since the last one, under the picture.

entries.title: Split screen opens without a flash
items: Opening split screen from the 2D tab no longer flashes a grey panel, and the layer tabs keep their names instead of blinking to img for a moment. The 2D view's background is black now, like the 3D view's.

entries.title: Chat emoji fit a narrow chat
items: Reacting in chat: the row of emoji opens above the button and stays inside the chat, so on a narrow chat the first ones are no longer cut off.

entries.title: Old notifications stay read
items: Notifications you had already read were showing as unread again since this afternoon. They are read again, and reading one in one Pyr tab now marks it read in your other tabs too.

entries.title: Claim the next 3 Quest cells at once
items: Quests: a Claim next 3 button in the Open list claims the next open cells in one press, up to the 3 you can hold, and opens the first.

entries.title: Clearer layer tabs, and four fixes
items: The selected layer tab is filled in more strongly, with its name in bold, so you can tell at a glance which one you are on.
Ask for Edit Access is now number 5 in the menu, straight after Advanced Interface.
Reacting to an announcement in chat: the row of emoji no longer runs off the left edge of the chat.
Notifications you had read no longer come back as unread.
Screenshot, whole screen: when drawing the page takes too long, the window now asks you to press Capture screen instead of failing with an error.

entries.title: Saves that fail are tried again
items: When the server does not answer, your splits, merges, completions and cell types now wait in your browser and are sent again until they go through, even after a reload. A small note at the bottom of the screen says Couldn't save, retrying, and then Saved.
Release Claim in the cell menu now says so when the release did not go through, instead of saying Released.

entries.title: Every key in one list
items: Press ? (or type keys in the Ctrl+K box) to see every key in Pyr, grouped as Moving around, Editing, Tools and Panels. Click one to try it. The menu has it too, under Keyboard shortcuts.
Commands found with Ctrl+K show their key on the right.

entries.title: Videos in notifications: Watch on YouTube
items: Under a video in a notification, the link now says Watch on YouTube (or Vimeo, or Google Drive) instead of the web address, and opens in a new tab.

entries.title: Q and W step through slices
items: The slice keys are now Q (back) and W (forward), not Z and X: Z is snap again, as it always was.

entries.title: Shift+Delete removes a cell
items: Point at a cell, in the 2D or 3D view or in the segment list, and press Shift+Delete to remove it from your list, as its trash button does. Ctrl+Z brings it back.

entries.title: Scheduled notifications show up
items: A notification the team wrote ahead of time now appears at the top of your bell when it goes out, with its picture in chat, instead of being lost further down.

entries.title: Hide announcements in chat
items: Announcements in chat, like Today in Pyr, have an × to hide them from your chat. They stay in your notifications.

entries.title: Z and X step through slices
items: Press Z and X to step back and forward one slice at a time, as COMMA and PERIOD do, so you can keep your other hand on the trackpad or mouse.

entries.title: EyeWire Radio plays in one tab at a time
items: With Pyr open in several tabs, only one plays EyeWire Radio. A new tab stays quiet while another is playing, and turning the radio on in a tab moves the music there.

entries.title: Right click works right up to the edge of the data
items: In the 2D view, a right click on a cell near the edge of the dataset moves you there again. Only clicks outside the data are ignored.

entries.title: Videos play inside notifications
items: A notification with a video link (YouTube, Vimeo, Google Drive or a video file) now plays the video right inside it when you open it.

entries.title: A steadier bottom of the screen in cut mode
items: When several messages come up in a row, as cut and merge errors can, only the newest shows, so the bars and the legend at the bottom stay where they are.
The big "Now press G" prompt in cut mode only shows during the Cut tutorial, not in your own cutting.

entries.title: Merge and cut mode carry on to your next cell
items: With merge or cut mode on, moving to your next cell (after completing one, claiming one, or a jump) used to leave the mode on screen but not working until you switched it off and on. It now works straight away in the new cell.

entries.title: A clearer middle for the cursor
items: The target cursor's lines now stay outside its circle, so only a small dot sits over what you are looking at.

entries.title: Tutorials mention the 2D EM tab
items: Get Started and Advanced Interface now say you can click the 2D EM tab, as well as press SPACE, to open the split screen.

entries.title: The 2D EM tab shows and hides 2D
items: Clicking the 2D EM tab at the top now switches the 2D view on and off: split screen or 3D only. Right click still turns the layer on and off. Its side panel is under Settings, Advanced.

entries.title: Right clicks stay inside the data
items: A right click in the 2D view on the box around a dataset, or out past it, no longer moves you there. Inside the data, a right click still moves the view to that spot.

entries.title: The hovered cell in 2D keeps your opacity
items: With the new 3D Hover looks, the cell under your mouse in 2D no longer turns almost solid: it keeps the opacity set in the Render tab.

entries.title: 2D images from Asia
items: Players in Asia can load the 2D images for EyeWire II, MEC and the Sandbox from a copy hosted in Asia, which is much faster there.
Settings has a new choice, 2D images load from: Automatic, Americas or Asia. Automatic checks once which copy is faster for you and uses it.
If your 2D images keep loading slowly and the Asia copy would be faster, Pyr offers to switch.

entries.title: Can't Complete no longer marks a cell proofread
items: Can't Complete no longer marks the cell proofread for the lab. It still ends your claim, counts as your completed cell, and records Can't Complete with your note in the cell sheet.
The Can't complete button in the Δ menu shows only on cells that are in the Cell Library's sheet.

entries.title: Can't complete in the Δ menu
items: The Δ menu of a Cell Library cell has a Can't complete button under Mark as Proofread. It opens the usual form with Can't Complete already chosen, so you only add why.

entries.title: A friendlier Merge Queue
items: In merge mode, each cell in the Merge Queue is shown in its own colour, as in the segment list.
Hovering a cell in the Merge Queue lights it up in the views, and right clicking it takes you to it.
With the Pulse hover look, a cell you point at in the segment list or the Merge Queue now glows in 3D.

entries.title: A smaller cursor on a laptop
items: On a laptop or a smaller window, the target cursor is a size smaller, so it does not cover the cell. Extra large cursor in Settings keeps its size.

entries.title: 3D Hover: a new Hologram
items: Hologram now turns the cell into cyan light, or your pulse colour: a bright body glowing brightest at its edges, a fine sprinkle of dots and a soft glow around it, instead of dark stripes.
New players now start with Spotlight. If you were already playing, your look stays as it was.

entries.title: A target cursor
items: A new cursor over the 2D and 3D views: a white target with a dark edge that is easy to spot on the EM images, and a little lighter over 3D. On a big screen, Settings has an Extra large cursor.
Right clicking the box drawn around a dataset no longer moves you to that box.

entries.title: Straight on to Merge
items: Get Started ends with a Start Merge button.
Leaving a tutorial reminds you that all the tutorials live in the hamburger menu.

entries.title: Cell types come back after a server hiccup
items: When the lab's server has a hiccup, cell types no longer look lost: Pyr keeps asking every 30 seconds and shows them again once the server answers.
The Δ menu says when it could not reach the lab's server to check a cell's type, instead of saying the cell has no type.

entries.title: Slim view: claim your next cell from the bar
items: The Cell Library's slim view arrow now always shrinks the library. With no cell to show yet, the slim bar offers Claim a new cell, which claims the next cell on the Available tab and takes you to it.
Finish your last claimed cell in slim view and the bar offers a new one, instead of opening the whole library.

entries.title: Your turn for the Proofreading Test, one click away
items: The notification that it is your turn for the Proofreading Test now opens the test when you click it.

entries.title: 3D Hover: Spotlight, Hologram and Metallic
items: Settings, 3D Hover has a new look, Spotlight: the cell under your mouse turns a little richer and the other cells in 3D dim, so it stands out gently.

Wireframe is now Hologram: the cell turns dark and glows from its edges in its own colour, with faint lines across it. It is as quick as the other looks. There is also Metallic, a dark, shiny cell with bright edges.

entries.title: Pictures in replies to your reports
items: When the team answers a report you sent, the answer can now come with a picture, like a screenshot of what they mean. Click it to see it full size.

entries.title: New players meet the top bar one tool at a time
items: A brand new player starts with only the bell in the top bar. Each tool arrives with the tutorial step that teaches it, and Nurro introduces the others.
Finishing Get Started brings the Leaderboard, Undelete and Chat, and the Merge tutorial starts by itself.
The Merge and Cut tutorials bring their tools, and finishing both brings the Cell Library.
Advanced Interface brings Find Path, Tags, Highlight and Lantern, and finishing it brings the Layer side panel.
Coming back on a second and third day fills in anything missed, and Your Week in Science arrives after a week.
Every tool is still in Profile, Settings, Toolbar Icons and in the Ctrl+K command bar, which now also opens Find Path, Highlight, Lantern, Undelete, Chat and more.
Players who already have an account keep their top bar exactly as it is.

entries.title: Settings use the whole screen
items: Profile Settings now use the full width of the profile.
Click a box's title in Settings to fold it away. Pyr remembers which ones you folded.

entries.title: Was your help request answered?
items: A day after someone replies to your help request, the bell asks whether it was answered, with a link that marks it solved right there.
Mark it solved before then and the question never comes. You only get it once per request.

entries.title: Advanced Interface: naming your layer
items: The step that asks you to name your new annotation layer now opens that layer's side panel, even when the layer was already selected.

entries.title: A tidier Layers list
items: The Layers list in the side panel matches the rest of Pyr: rounded rows, small numbers, and the layer you have selected marked in blue.

entries.title: A Help tab you can read
items: Help requests, replies and their buttons use larger text, and screenshots show at twice the size.
A long note says Show more, and opens in place.
Mark solved, which used to say Resolve, shows only for the player who asked and for admins, so nobody closes a request by mistake.

entries.title: A line for the Proofreading Test
items: When someone else is taking the Proofreading Test, its first box has Join the line. A card at the top left shows your place and a rough wait.
When the cell frees up, the first in line gets a notification, and the card says it is your turn: the cell is held for you for 10 minutes.
While anyone is waiting, the player on the cell keeps it through 15 quiet minutes instead of an hour.

entries.title: Proofreading Test: a way out
items: The bar at the top left of the Proofreading Test has Leave, to hand the cell back without a score, and its help card uses the same lettering as the rest of Pyr.

entries.title: Proofreading Test: not open yet
items: The Proofreading Test in the menu now says DO NOT TAKE. It is still being built and tried by the team; we will say when it is ready for you.

entries.title: Funnier Achievements, and the Ultramicrotome
items: Every Cell Completion and Editor Achievement now has its own line in your Trophy Case, most of them jokes, written by Celia and the Pyr team.

The Cell Completion Achievement for 2,000 cells is now the Ultramicrotome, the machine that slices brain tissue thin enough to image every cell. If you already have it, you keep it, with its new picture.

entries.title: Tidier corners
items: The music button sits in the bottom right corner of the 3D view, with the Sections box beside it, and no longer floats up when a message bar shows along the bottom.
Hovering the x, y and z letters in a view's corner opens a tidy card for the view's scale, with tips on what Default and Zoom-relative do.

entries.title: The 3D view no longer zooms out of sight
items: Scrolling in the 3D view can no longer zoom out so far that your cells disappear. Some mice in Firefox sent such big scroll steps that a few notches left the 3D view empty.
A view saved zoomed out that far now opens at the dataset's normal 3D distance.

entries.title: 3D Hover: None, and a gentler Saturate
items: Settings, 3D Hover now has None, for no highlight on the cell under your mouse. Pressing P still makes a cell pulse.
Saturate is gentler, so the cell keeps its shading.

entries.title: A pumpkin patch in the Sandbox
items: For Halloween, three cells in the Sandbox wear jack o' lanterns over their cell bodies in the 3D view, and their branches grow out through the faces. They stay until 1 November.

The pumpkin button beside the emoji button in chat has news of a rare cell type, and takes you to see it. On a pumpkin cell, the same button takes the pumpkins off and puts them back. You can also turn them off in Settings.

entries.title: Photo mode
items: Photo mode hides everything but the 3D view, fills the window with it and turns your cells slowly, like a turntable. Open it from Just for fun in the menu, from the row of buttons that appears after Share, or from the command palette.

Its small bar picks the spin speed and a black, night, grey or white background, saves a clean picture, and records one full turn as a short video you can share. Esc leaves and puts your view back as it was.
Pick centre chooses what the spin turns around: click a spot on a cell, or type a point as x, y, z.

entries.title: 3D Hover: Halo, Pulse, Wireframe and Saturate
items: New 3D Hover looks for the cell under your mouse, in Settings under 3D Hover: Halo, a slim glowing line around the cell; Pulse, a ring of light running out along the cell from your mouse when you point at it, in a colour you choose; Wireframe, the cell's 3D mesh drawn in glowing lines, finer as you zoom in; and Saturate, the cell's colour turning richer and lit from within instead of paler.
Press P with your mouse over a cell in 3D to send a ring of light along it, whichever look you use. The pulse colour can be any colour you like.
New players start with Halo. If you were already playing, the original look stays until you pick another.
With the new looks, the cell under your mouse in 2D keeps its own colour and turns more solid instead of fading to white.
Keep my display settings now also keeps Highlight on hover the way you set it when you jump to another cell.

entries.title: A roomier slim Cell Library
items: The slim Cell Library bar is wider, so your cell's whole ID shows, and it keeps the Cell Library's neuron.
The arrow that shrinks and opens the Cell Library is on the left in both views, and the next cell arrow is on the right.
Shrinking and opening the Cell Library and the Highlight box is one light bar that zips up and down, with rounded corners.
The Cell Library's settings and close buttons are bigger.

entries.title: A shorter Submit an issue
items: Submit an issue now asks for just one line: in a few words, what is it.
Want to say more? Click Add details.

entries.title: Cut points as small as merge points
items: Cut mode's Points sizes are now Small, Medium and Large, and Small is the same size as a merge point, for the tiniest pieces. The cut points no longer grow with your annotation size.

entries.title: Tidier Segments panel and Cell Library rows
items: Cells in a folder keep their jump arrow beside the ID instead of dropping to a second line.
The remove button on Pasted is no longer pushed off the edge of the panel.
The cell type list in the Complete form opens dark, like the rest of the panel.
Cell Library rows: the AI's type stays on one line, and the green bar alone marks the cell you are viewing.

entries.title: A cleaner tutorial pointer
items: Tutorial boxes now point with a thin line and a lit dot on what they mean.

entries.title: A title on every report
items: Submit an issue now asks for a short title, so the team sees at a glance what your report is about.
The Data problem choice is gone. Pick Bug, Idea or Other.

entries.title: Folders you can size, and a longer notifications window
items: Drag the grip under a folder in the Segments panel to make it taller or shorter. Double click the grip to give it its usual size.
+ Folder beside Move down puts your pasted cells straight into a new folder.
The Segments panel's green is now sky blue.
Drag the bottom edge of the notifications window to make it longer, and press Show more to see older notifications.

entries.title: What the AI predicts for each cell
items: On the Retina, each cell in the Cell Library shows the bipolar type the lab's AI predicts for it, for example 6 bipolar (t6), and so does the Cell Profile.
When you complete a cell the AI's type stands. If you are sure it is wrong, press Wrong? Correct it and choose the right one.

entries.title: Pasted coordinates find their cell
items: Coordinates pasted into the Segments box now find the cell there right away, without opening the 2D view.
Find Path failure messages go away by themselves.
Advanced Interface: clearer steps for hiding a layer, rows, Lantern and Find Path, and a shorter final mission.

entries.title: Several Pyr tabs at once
items: With Pyr open in more than one tab, each tab now keeps track of its own claimed cell, so moving to another cell in one tab no longer saves that tab's view into the cell you are working on in the other.
A setting you change in one tab now reaches your other open tabs too, instead of being put back by them.
If your graphics card runs short and the views stop drawing, which can happen with several tabs open, a notice offers to reload that tab.

entries.title: Smaller cut points
items: Cut mode has a Points choice beside Keep open: Small, Medium, Regular or Large. It sizes only the red and blue cut points, so your annotation layers keep their own size.

entries.title: The Sandbox opens with its cells
items: Opening Pyr at its plain address shows the Sandbox's starting cells again, as switching to the Sandbox does.

entries.title: Progress toward your next badge
items: The progress bars toward your next edits and cells badges now start from the last badge your count has passed, so they no longer show a negative percentage.

entries.title: Type a cell as you complete it
items: The Cell Library's Complete form now has an optional Cell type: pick from the list or type your own, and it is saved together with the completion, so there is no separate step in the Cell Profile.

entries.title: Boxes, circles, arrows and text on screenshots
items: When you mark up a screenshot you can now draw a box, a circle or an arrow, and add text you can drag into place, as well as using the pen.
Hold Shift to draw a perfect square or circle.

entries.title: The 2D view no longer freezes
items: After switching between 2D only and 2D + 3D, or after moving on to your next cell, the 2D view sometimes stopped loading new slices until you pressed Space twice or reloaded. It now keeps loading.

entries.title: Your profile fits a smaller screen
items: On a laptop screen, or with the browser zoomed in, your profile now fits the window, with its close button in the corner where you can reach it.

entries.title: New full screen and split screen buttons
items: With a mouse, the corner buttons of the 2D and 3D views are now icons in the style of the rest of Pyr, and each spells out what it does when you point at it: 3D only, 2D only, or 2D + 3D to come back to split screen.

entries.title: Your profile opens without a jump
items: Your profile builds from the top down: each row appears whole, with its line, numbers and curve, once its numbers are in, instead of pieces landing as they arrive. Nothing shifts.
The light that ran around the edge of the profile is gone, now that the profile fills the window.
The browser tab now says Pyr, not neuroglancer.
In the Trophy Case the tiles show each Achievement's name and threshold; its description shows when you pick it.

entries.title: Numbered annotations, in folders
items: Every annotation in a layer's list now has a number, in the list's order.
+ Folder makes a folder for your annotations. Name it, fold it, put one folder inside another, or delete it.
Drag an annotation's row to move it up or down the list, or onto a folder to put it in.
Ctrl+click or Shift+click picks several annotations to move to a folder or delete together.
Pick a color on a folder's dot to draw its annotations in that color. Untick Color its annotations to give them the layer's color again.
Your order and folders are saved with the layer, so saved views and shared links keep them.

entries.title: A way back from 3D only
items: After you switch to 3D only, a 2D + 3D button in the corner of the 3D view brings the 2D image back. Space still does the same.

entries.title: Proofreading Test results, biggest misses first
items: The Proofreading Test, still a work in progress, now lists your biggest misses first and pins at most 25 of them on the cell, so a long list stays readable.

entries.title: What a connectome is, in Get Started
items: Page 2 of the Get Started tutorial now says what a connectome is, with a link to Connectome 101.

entries.title: Tidier Segments panel on tablets
items: On a tablet the Segments panel buttons no longer pile up on top of the first cell after a split, a merge or a tap.
Each cell's remove button is now at the far right of its row, right under the heading's remove all.
In the report form, the box for console messages is greyed out when there are none to send.

entries.title: Pasted coordinates show their cell
items: Coordinates pasted into the Segments box stay there while the cell is found, and the new row shows where it came from.
Tutorial boxes point with a tab from their own edge and open in place.
Advanced Interface asks you to try a step before skipping it, and adds a second Highlight color.

entries.title: The Sandbox opens close in
items: The Sandbox's 2D view now opens close enough in for its cells to load.
In Advanced Interface, the arrow settles after two sweeps, Checked highlights show pink, and the memo opens the Segments tab.

entries.title: A new Advanced Interface tutorial
items: Advanced Interface is rebuilt in four short parts: marking what you see, working with cells, finding your way, and putting it together to find where a merger starts.
The tutorials now run Get Started, Merge, Cut, Advanced Interface, then the Merger Sandbox.
Tutorial boxes sit right next to what they point at, with a new arrow, copy buttons for coordinates and IDs, and hints you can hover.
Many steps move on by themselves when you do the thing they ask.
New annotation layers start with golden Pyr gems.
The Render tab is split into Colors, 2D view, 3D view and More, each with its own Opacity.
Pasting coordinates into the Segments box opens the 2D view close in, so the cell there is found.
Opening Highlight closes Find Path, and Submit stops pulsing once a path is found.
The menu closes when you click outside it.
In the Sandbox, 2D EM and 3D segmentation can no longer be removed by accident.
Chat no longer opens below the screen after a reload, and the Quest ID check shows the full ID.

entries.title: An easier to spot search box in Segments
items: The box at the top of the Segments panel, where you paste cell IDs or coordinates or search by name, now looks like a box to type in, with more room around it.

entries.title: A cleaner annotation layer panel
items: An annotation layer's panel now shows its name at the top like a file name. Click the pencil (or the name) to rename it.
The tools start right under the name, and the delete button turns red when you point at it.
Settings for filtering annotations by linked cells are under Advanced at the bottom of the panel.

entries.title: Cut mode keeps your cells on screen
items: Pressing C no longer hides the cells you are working on to show some old cell. Cut points left on a cell you are not showing, from an earlier visit or a saved view, are cleared as cut mode opens, and the cut bar offers Undo for a few seconds.
A cell with cut points on it can now be hidden or removed while cut mode is closed. Before, it kept coming back.
Ask for Edit Access: a cut example saves only while the cell its points are on is shown, so the reviewer sees the cell with the points.

entries.title: Quests load all day
items: The quest list no longer stops loading partway through the day with a Too Many Requests error. It had a daily limit that was far too low for busy questers.

entries.title: A tidier Learn more menu
items: The old Proofreading Guide link is gone from the menu and the command search, because it no longer matched Pyr. The tutorials in the menu cover everything it did.

entries.title: Tablets: back to 2D with 3D, and a tidy Segments heading
items: On a tablet, choosing 3D only now leaves a 2D + 3D button to go back, and split screen has 2D only and 3D only buttons.
On a touch screen the In view heading in the Segments panel no longer stacks Select on top of the count, so Select works with one tap.

entries.title: Ask for Edit Access, right in Pyr
items: You can now ask for edit access to the retina inside the game: open the menu and choose Ask for Edit Access, at the very bottom.
Place cut or merge points on ten mistakes you find, without submitting the edits, and save each view with one click. Pyr keeps every point and your notes.
Send all ten for review. The team looks at every point and answers in your notifications, with notes on each example.
Change any example before or after you send, as often as you like. You are never locked out.
Press Slim to make the box small on a laptop screen.

entries.title: Open a cell from chat in a new tab
items: A cell ID in chat is now a link: right click it and open it in a new tab, or middle click or Ctrl click it, to look at the cell without leaving what you are doing. A plain click still jumps to it here.
If you minimize the chat, it stays minimized after you reload Pyr.

entries.title: Claimed cells stay the cell you claimed
items: After you edit a cell you claimed, completing it no longer says the cell is not in the sheet, and the claim no longer turns into a neighbouring cell.
Claims already affected are put back to their own cell the next time you open the Cell Library.

entries.title: Tidier Segments headings, and a safer folder delete
items: Every heading in the Segments panel reads the same way: the eye on the left, in line with the cells' eyes, then the name and count, and a folder's color dot on the right above the cells' status marks.
Hover a heading for its buttons. The ones that remove things sit last on the right, set apart by a thin line, and the trash can is red so it never looks like copy.
A folder's ✕ asks what to do: keep its cells in view, remove only the hidden ones, or remove them all with the folder. Enter keeps them.
A long cell ID ends in … on hover so the buttons never sit on top of it, and each folder's colored line now starts at its heading.

entries.title: No more grey flashes when scrolling through slices
items: When you scroll through slices in the 2D view, the picture no longer goes grey for a moment every 16 slices. It now shows a blurry version straight away and sharpens as it loads.

entries.title: Completion messages in front of the Cell Library
items: The card after you submit a quest cell, and the messages after you complete a cell, now show in front of the Cell Library instead of behind it.

entries.title: Calm screen
items: A new setting, Calm screen: no animations or glows. It is in Settings, under User Interface. It stops the animations, takes away the glows and the twinkling dots, and makes your profile plainer. Your cells and the 3D view stay as they are.
A special award you receive now shows on your profile the next time you open it, without reloading Pyr.

entries.title: Quest layers stay with their quests
items: Looking at any cell from the Cell Library, or opening one of your claimed cells, now puts the quest's annotation layers away first, even in a new tab. They no longer show up on other cells or get saved into a claimed cell's view.

entries.title: Profile curves: none on small screens, a settled draw on large ones
items: On a laptop or a small screen zoomed in, your profile shows the numbers without the curves. The curves stay on larger screens.
On larger screens each curve now draws once after the frame has settled, instead of snapping to its end a moment in.

entries.title: Lists in team replies
items: Replies from the team about your reports now show their numbered and bulleted lists as lists.

entries.title: Easier on phones and tablets
items: Swiping one finger through the 2D images moves through the slices more slowly, so you can stop where you want.
Hold one finger still on a spot to move the view there. It now takes just over half a second.
On a touch screen the Segments panel has a Select button: tap cells to pick them, then move them to a folder, show, hide, color or remove them together.
On a phone the corner button switches between 3D only and 2D with 3D.

entries.title: Quest work stays with its quest cell
items: Jumping from a quest cell to one of your claimed cells now saves your quest work first and takes the quest's layers out of the view. Before, they came along, and your quest cell could reopen showing the wrong cell.

entries.title: Restore all settings to default
items: Settings has a new button at the bottom, Restore all settings to default. It asks first, then puts every setting back to how Pyr starts, on all your computers. Your flag, bio, cells and progress stay as they are.

entries.title: A new Segments panel, with folders
items: The Seg. tab is now called Segments, rebuilt to make your cells easier to manage.
Paste cell IDs into the box to add them straight to your view, under Pasted. Paste coordinates to go there and add the cell at that spot.
Make folders to group your cells: drag cells onto a folder, fold it away, put folders inside folders, and drag folders to reorder them.
Click a folder's color dot to give every cell in it one color. A checkbox lets cells you add later take that color too.
Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on a Mac) or Shift+click to pick several cells, then move, show, hide, color or remove them together from the bar at the bottom.
Click a cell's ID to open its menu. The trash can on a row removes that cell from your view; the one on a heading removes them all after asking, and Shift+click removes only the hidden ones.
Type a name like Pyramidal to find your cells by type.
The bounding box controls and the Select tool are in the Render tab, and the cell layer's panel shows its name and a close button only.

entries.title: A new Müller cell in Meet the cells
items: Retina's Meet the cells tour now shows a single Müller glia cell. The one before was two cells stuck together.
In the Cilia Quest, the explanation for No cilium (BB & DC clear) is clearer: the centrioles are visible and clearly differentiated, with the basal body closer to the surface.

entries.title: Choose how sharp the 2D images are
items: A new setting, 2D image detail, lets you draw the 2D images at Half or Quarter detail so they load much faster on a slow connection. It is in Settings, under User Interface. Full stays the default, and your choice is kept on your account.

entries.title: Your viewer settings stay put
items: Prefetching, concurrent chunk requests and the memory limits you set in Viewer settings are now kept on your account. Opening a quest cell, a link or reloading no longer puts them back to the defaults.

entries.title: Lighter on the server
items: The leaderboard refreshes every two minutes instead of every minute, and asks for far less each time. Opening a player's card loads their all-time totals.
The bell checks for new notifications once a minute and asks only for what is new. A new notification still appears within a minute.

entries.title: Tap to place on phones and tablets
items: On a touch screen, one tap now places a point in Cut, Merge and Find Path, the same as Ctrl+click. Two quick taps still show or hide a cell.
One tap also places annotation points, and Highlight points while the Highlight box is open.
On a touch screen the Cut and Merge bar says tap and shows buttons in place of keys.

entries.title: Tablets keep the top bar during Cut and Merge
items: On a tablet, starting Cut or Merge from the top bar no longer slides the whole page up and hides the top bar.

entries.title: Cell Profile on the right, steadier chat scrolling
items: The Cell Profile opens along the right edge of the page instead of over the cells you are looking at. Close it with its X or by clicking outside it.
Scrolling to the top of the chat loads one page of older messages at a time, so a quick swipe no longer races far back. Scroll up again to see more.

entries.title: Cell Profile and reply screenshots
items: The Cell Profile opens over the side panel and has its own X to close it. Clicking outside it still closes it too.
A screenshot you add to a reply now stays attached. Clicking in the screenshot window used to close the reply and lose the picture.

entries.title: Your Cilia Quest work is kept
items: The quest you are working on is marked Active in the Quests tab, and each of your quests shows its cell ID.

Your annotations on a quest are saved as you place them. Open on the quest you are on goes to the cell without reloading it, and opening one of your quests again brings your saved work back. Save now saves it at once.

entries.title: See the segment ID under a cell's label
items: A new setting, Show the segment ID under a cell's label, writes each typed cell's segment ID under its label in the segment list. It is in Settings, under User Interface, and is off unless you turn it on.

entries.title: Your work is kept when CAVE is down
items: When CAVE is not answering, marking a cell proofread or saving a cell type no longer asks you to try again. Pyr keeps it, counts it right away, and sends it to CAVE as soon as CAVE is back, under your name.
You will see a message when something is waiting, and another when it has been sent. Unmarking a cell before then simply takes it off the list.
Replying to the team now ends on the lit up neuron alone.

entries.title: Jumps take you straight to the cell
items: Jumping to a cell on another dataset, from chat, the Cell Library or My cells, now shows just that cell, without the dataset's starter cells, and no longer reloads the page on the way.

entries.title: Easier 3D controls
items: In the 3D view, scroll now zooms in and out, and dragging with the right mouse button slides the view. A right click without dragging still centres the view where you clicked.
Ctrl+scroll and Shift+drag keep working too, so use whichever you like. The 2D views are unchanged: scroll still moves through the sections.
Retina opens on two current cells, in blue and gold.
You can wave in chat: 👋 is now in the emoji choices.
The music button sits beside the 3D view's Sections box instead of above it, and the green segment colour is a softer green.
Your profile shows your latest 10 completed cells, with the rest a click away in My cells, and cells finished from the Cell Library show their segment ID.

entries.title: Your profile lists only your own completed cells
items: Recently completed cells on a profile now lists the cells that player completed. Before, it could show cells completed by someone else who had used the same browser.

entries.title: Music on, and replies that show they arrived
items: Pyr Radio now plays when you start, unless you have turned it off. If you turn it off, it stays off.
The music button sits on the same line as the coordinates, and moves up only when something is under it.
Replying to the team shows each step while it sends, then lets you know the team has it.

entries.title: The Proofreading Test gets a clock
items: The Proofreading Test, still a work in progress, has a 60 minute time limit. The time left shows at the top left, and when it runs out your cell is scored as it stands.

entries.title: Tutorials menu numbers line up
items: The numbers in the Tutorials menu now line up in one column on the left.
The Proofreading Test, still a work in progress, shows a loading card while it gets your cell and while it scores, and gives you an End layer with Pyr gems for marking branch ends.

entries.title: The Proofreading Test is marked WIP
items: The Proofreading Test in the Tutorials menu now says WIP, for work in progress. It is still being tried out, so please leave it for now.

entries.title: Cut tutorial: two points on each side
items: The first cut in the Cut tutorial now asks for 2 red and 2 blue points. With one point a side the cut took only half the axon off.
If a cut there leaves half the axon attached, the box says so and shows where the rest goes.
Pressing C or M a second time now says the tool is off, and how to turn it back on.
Small wording changes from tester feedback.

entries.title: Cut tutorial: half a cut is not the whole job
items: In the 2D cut of the Cut tutorial, cutting the axon off only partway no longer counts. The box says half is done and shows where the rest of the cut goes.
Practice views no longer show every hint point twice.

entries.title: Merge tutorial: the second merge shows where to click
items: The second merge in the Merge tutorial now shows pink gems on the two spots to click, as the first one does.

entries.title: Chat keeps working when live updates are down
items: If the live connection behind chat goes down, you can still read and send messages. New ones arrive every few seconds, and the dot at the top of chat turns amber until the live connection is back.

entries.title: The Cilia Quest
items: The Cell Library has a Quests tab. On Retina, claim a starburst cell, mark its basal body, daughter centriole and cilium centerline in the layers that open with it, and press Submit. The cell does not need to be proofread. You can hold three cells at a time.

Your answer, your notes and a share link of your view go to the lab's sheet with your name and the date. Submitting brings a celebration and your count, and your profile shows how many quests you have completed.

Annotation layers have a new tool, the polyline: hold Ctrl and click along a line, press Enter to finish, Backspace to take a point back, Esc to cancel. It is the same polyline the lab's own viewer draws.

The quest's Instructions link the lab's guide, its training video and a reference: three real example cells, annotated by the lab, each saying which status it shows and when to use it. In any annotation list, a description now shows in full where it used to be cut at one line.

entries.title: Reply to the team with a screenshot
items: When the team asks you for a reply about a report, you can now add a screenshot, your current view and your recent console messages, the same as on a report.
The screenshot shows the game, not the message you are answering.

entries.title: Preview a cut before you make it
items: In cut mode, place your red and blue points and press Preview. The cell is coloured in 3D to show what would stay with the red points and what would go with the blue ones, so you can see where the cut will fall before you make it.
Around your points the colours follow the supervoxels themselves, so the edge of the cut is exact there. Farther along the cell they show which side each branch ends up on.
Nothing is cut until you press Submit cut. The colours go away when you move a point, submit, or leave cut mode.

entries.title: Reply to the team about your report
items: When the team asks you a question about a report you sent, the notification now has a box where you can write back.

entries.title: Pyr gems stay on your annotation layers
items: When you set an annotation layer to show its points as Pyr gems, the layer of the same name on the next cell you open shows gems too. Before, it went back to dots with every new cell.

entries.title: Steadier segment list, and help requests read better in chat
items: Removing a segment no longer flashes a bar along the bottom, so the legend under the list stays still.
After you click the legend, pressing Enter to send a merge or a cut no longer starts a legend check.
The cell menu shows how many claims you really have left, counting cells claimed in the Cell Library.
A help request shows in chat as New help request from the player, without the SOS emoji.

entries.title: The profile keeps its shape on a very wide screen
items: On a very wide screen the profile overview no longer stretches across the whole window: it keeps the proportions it has on a normal screen and sits in the middle of the frame.
In each row of your profile, the count of what is left to your next Achievement now sits above the arrow to the Trophy Case, where the row ends, instead of at the far edge of the window.

entries.title: Retina: a claimed cell shows WIP in the sheet
items: When you claim a Retina cell, its Status in the sheet is set to WIP, so you can see in the sheet which cells are yours to do.
Completing the cell replaces WIP with the status you choose. Releasing it clears WIP along with your name.

entries.title: New annotation layers open at your point size
items: A new annotation layer you make now opens at the size you last set on the Size slider, and the Annotate point button keeps that size.

entries.title: Your annotation point size is remembered
items: Set the Size slider on an annotation layer once, and new annotation layers and new workspaces open at that size. A layer keeps its own size if you set one for it.

entries.title: Shift+L opens and closes the Cell Library
items: Press Shift+L to open and close the Cell Library. The shortcut is now shown when you hover its icon in the top bar and its close button.

entries.title: Cells the lab finished are not offered again
items: On Retina, a cell the lab's own sheet marks as complete no longer offers Mark as Proofread or Claim in its Delta menu. The menu says the lab has already proofread it.
A cell you completed in Pyr keeps its Unmark, and a cell you already hold keeps its Release.

entries.title: Dots for your Merger Sandbox progress
items: Your progress in the Merger Sandbox is shown as plain dots in the full box too.

entries.title: Skip sits beside Help me
items: In the Merger Sandbox, Skip is now a button to the left of Help me.

entries.title: Skip, when there is nothing to skip to
items: Skipping your last unsolved merger used to show it as still fused. Skip this one now only appears when there is another merger to go to.

entries.title: Merger Sandbox: Next is the main button again
items: The main button in the Merger Sandbox is Next, which checks your cut. Skip this one is a small link in the full box.
The slim bar opens a line of text when there is news, such as a cut that went through but did not finish the job.
The slim bar shows your progress as plain dots.

entries.title: Notices at the bottom no longer cover the legend
items: When a notice or tool bar runs along the bottom of the screen, the segment list legend and the Sections switch in the 3D view move up so you can still see and use them.

entries.title: The slim Merger Sandbox box is one bar
items: Folded, the Merger Sandbox box is now a single bar: your progress and Skip. Open it again with the small arrow for the hint and Help me.

entries.title: Retina cells show what the lab knows
items: On Retina, a cell the lab's own sheet lists now shows it in the segment list: its mark says proofread, typed or done, and its class and type stand in for its ID.
The Delta menu fills in the same way. Completion Status and Cell Type say what the lab's sheet says wherever nothing is saved in Pyr yet, and the menu's title is the cell's class and type.
What you save in Pyr always wins, and the lab's sheet does not change your stats.
